The search giant is revamping Google.com with AI options.

This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more users to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of new features worldwide.

The new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the new buttons when signed in to my Google account.

When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

Clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a new page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”

The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

Another new feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which shows your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:

Stein said the new sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other new AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion users in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the company’s “fastest growing product ever.”

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The New York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Google said search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

Google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

#3092. I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site or when you click to or take an action on their website. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Some of the best Southwest redemptions are only available if you hold one of the airline’s credit cards.

In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

Take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

"Experiences create lifetime memories,” says Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”

Southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but big-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.)

As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

$1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.)

Four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.)

If you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

Using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

Daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

Ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

Again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

Grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

The biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

With that said, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

Scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.)

Finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

Personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” says Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

#3091. Verizon Pays Out $11.7 Billion a Year in Dividends. Here’s the Free Cash Flow Math Behind Its 6.2%-Yielding Payout.

By Matt DiLallo – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:03PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Verizon Communications ›

Verizon (VZ +1.62%) pays $0.7075 per share in dividends to its investors each quarter. At its recent share price, the telecom giant yields 6.2%, significantly higher than the S&P 500's 1.1%. Verizon's dividend costs about $2.9 billion per quarter, or around $11.7 billion annually.

Here's a look at the free cash flow that supports its high-yielding dividend.

Verizon generates substantial recurring revenue as customers pay their internet and broadband bills. It hauled in $34.3 billion of revenue during the third quarter, up 1.5% year over year. It has generated $103 billion of revenue during the first nine months of this year (up 1.2%).

The company converts a significant portion of its revenue into cash flow. Verizon generated $29.9 billion of cash flow from operations during the first nine months of this year, up nearly 7% compared to the year-ago period. The telecom giant spent $11.9 billion on capital expenditures to maintain and expand its networks, leaving it with $18 billion in free cash flow. That's up from $15.8 billion compared to the prior-year period. It was more than enough to cover the $8.8 billion Verizon paid in dividends. The company used its excess free cash flow to repurchase $4 billion of shares and strengthen its balance sheet.

Verizon currently expects to spend $16 billion to $16.5 billion on capital expenditures this year, down from $17 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, it now expects its free cash flow to increase by as much as 12% from last year's $20.1 billion, implying roughly $22.5 billion. That will cover its $11.7 billion in dividends nearly two times over.

That gives Verizon plenty of room to grow its dividend. The company delivered its 20th consecutive annual dividend increase earlier this year. It has been growing its payout at a modest low-single-digit rate, which should continue. That would still leave it with ample excess free cash flow to repurchase shares while continuing to strengthen its balance sheet. Verizon's debt has increased by $20 billion over the past year due to its acquisition of Frontier. However, it has a reasonable 2.3x leverage ratio (up from 2.2x in the year-ago period) and solid credit ratings (A-/BBB+/Baa1).

At over 6%, Verizon has one of the highest dividend yields in the S&P 500. However, it's not a high-risk dividend stock. The company comfortably covers its payout with cash, providing it with excess to strengthen its already solid balance sheet and repurchase shares. While Verizon won't provide much growth, it can certainly provide investors with a lucrative, steadily rising stream of passive dividend income.

#3090. New Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Debuts With 53 Mpg, AI in the Dash

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The redesigned compact sedan features Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant, Gleo AI, and an updated regenerative braking system with EV-like one-pedal driving.

Hyundai pulled back the cover on the new 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

An updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a new Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the new nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

Pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai says the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

“Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” said Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the new Elantra is anything but bland.

The sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

The sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

#3088. What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Electronics, small appliances, toys and clothes make the list, along with some out-of-the-box buys.

Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The big day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.)

You don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, says Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”

Non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

NeeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold says.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

“Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley says.

Got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

“Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

Electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

Gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”

That said, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold says.

For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, says consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

“Big-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

Many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold says. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”

One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch says.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch says. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.)

Check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”

Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

#3087. If You’d Invested $10,000 in Rocket Lab 5 Years Ago, Here’s How Much You’d Have Today -- Even After a 60% Crash

SpaceX is the industry leader, but Rocket Lab is proving that there's room for more than one space company.

By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:23PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›

Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%) have fallen roughly 60% from their all-time highs in June 2026. That's a massive decline. And yet, even with that decline, a $10,000 investment in the stock five years ago would still be worth more than $33,000 as of this writing. There's an important backstory here, even as Space Exploration Corporation (SPCX -7.69%) makes the biggest headlines in the still-emerging space industry. Here's what you need to know.

Benjamin Graham, the man who helped train Wall Street icon Warren Buffett, liked to say that Wall Street was a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term. The point here is that emotions are what move stock prices in the near term, while business success is recognized over the long term. Graham and Buffett both used this insight to highlight value investments, but it is equally important when considering growth stocks, assuming you have a long enough investment horizon.

That fact is on clear display in the space industry. There was massive enthusiasm for space-related stocks leading up to SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO). That enthusiasm petered out after the IPO. That's not particularly shocking, given the hype on Wall Street and Main Street around that IPO. Rocket Lab simply got caught up in the emotional swing since it is a SpaceX competitor. But that doesn't mean Rocket Lab isn't achieving success as a business.

Recent news was flooded with results from SpaceX's Starship launch. On the negative side, the company failed to catch the spaceship's lower section (the booster rocket). On the positive side, it successfully caught the upper portion (the actual spacecraft). The end goal is to have a completely reusable rocket system, which would dramatically reduce the cost of getting to space. It is very exciting stuff.

In the shadow of this industry leader, Rocket Lab achieved its own milestone on Nov. 14, 2026. That was the day the company marked the 100th launch of its Electron spacecraft. The company noted in a press release that it had set "a new record for reaching 100 launches faster than any other commercially developed rocket." SpaceX gets most of the headlines, but Rocket Lab is making progress as a business, too.

To be fair, Rocket Lab is a money-losing start-up. So it isn't an appropriate investment for risk-averse investors. But it may be of interest to growth investors that have a long-term focus. The space industry is still in its early stages of development. SpaceX is the dominant player, but there will be room for more than one company.

That's been highlighted recently by SpaceX's own satellite launch plans, which are limiting other companies' access to its launches. If the company increasingly focuses on its own business, it leaves companies with no other option but to turn to competitors like Rocket Lab. And given the success Rocket Lab has had with its own launches, investors are clearly recognizing the long-term opportunity even as emotional investors create material price volatility. That's why the stock is up so much over the long term but down so much over the short term.

Rocket Lab isn't for the faint of heart, given that the stock is likely to remain volatile. And operating in the shadow of SpaceX won't help the situation any. However, Rocket Lab is making important progress as a business. Over the long term, assuming you can handle the volatility, it could be an attractive option in the still-emerging space industry.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates rose enough today that you might be feeling some sticker shock.

If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

#3084. Asked on Reddit: I Lost My Job; What Should I Do First?

Income loss is stressful; the first steps involve cutting costs and focusing on essentials.

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

Should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any big moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

That’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he says. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a new policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your new job search — is also an important part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty says.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

At the same time, it’s important to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage company, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

“Having that release is mentally a big thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, says Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

People often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she says.

Starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine says. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something new also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so plan accordingly.

All three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

The Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

#3083. Prediction: This Will Be Nvidia’s Stock Price in 2027 After Its Phenomenal Q3 Results

Nvidia's latest results indicate that its impressive growth is sustainable.

By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:47PM EST

Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) has been in the news for the wrong reasons lately. However, the company put any concerns about its growth trajectory to rest following the release of its fiscal third-quarter results (for the three months ended Oct. 25) on Nov. 17.

The semiconductor giant didn't just crush Wall Street's expectations, but it also delivered stronger-than-expected guidance. Let's take a closer look at Nvidia's results and guidance to see whether this semiconductor stock can regain its mojo and jump higher over the coming year.

Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang recently resigned as CEO under unceremonious circumstances. CFO Colette Kress now heads the company in an interim capacity, while the search for a permanent CEO continues.

The company's solid results should assuage investors' concerns about its future during this uncertain time as it undergoes a transition. Nvidia's revenue shot up by 103% from the year-ago period to $115.8 billion in fiscal Q3, exceeding the $109.1 billion consensus estimate. Its non-GAAP earnings per share increased by 111% year over year to $2.68, beating the $2.48 estimate.

The guidance clearly suggests that the recent developments at Nvidia won't be hurting its dominance in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market. The company anticipates $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter, and this estimate excludes sales to Chinese customers. Wall Street would have settled for $125.1 billion in guidance.

Nvidia's guidance implies a 91% year-over-year increase in revenue. That's stronger than the 73% revenue increase the company reported in the same quarter last year. What's more, Kress noted on the latest earnings call that Nvidia's revenue will increase by 75% in fiscal 2028 (which begins in late January next year).

The company had previously anticipated a 70% increase in fiscal 2028 revenue, though it noted that the outlook was supply-constrained. It now expects stronger growth owing to rising demand for its chips and the company's ability to secure additional supply.

Even better, Nvidia sees an improvement in its margin profile in fiscal 2028. Kress pointed out that the company's gross margin will bottom in the current quarter and improve to the 72%-73% range in the next fiscal year. The company expects a non-GAAP gross margin of 72% in the current quarter, indicating it can deliver healthy earnings growth next year on the back of a strong top-line jump.

The fiscal 2028 guidance was the icing on the cake for Nvidia, as investor confidence would have taken a big hit had it scrapped the same. However, the better-than-expected guidance indicates that the company's growth story remains intact amid the ongoing transition. Also, a potential margin improvement should help Nvidia deliver strong earnings growth next year, which could send the stock soaring.

Nvidia stock has performed poorly on the market this year, and recent developments at the company have cast a cloud of negativity over it. However, the latest results and guidance should bring the stock out of the rut it is in.

Nvidia has generated $293.7 billion in revenue in the first nine months of fiscal 2027. Its fiscal Q4 guidance indicates that it will end the year with almost $424 billion in revenue. That implies a 96% jump over its fiscal 2026 revenue. The company's top line could reach $742 billion next year, based on the 75% jump it is forecasting for fiscal 2028.

Nvidia trades at 10 times sales, a premium to the U.S. technology sector's price-to-sales ratio of 6. However, its outstanding growth justifies that premium. Assuming Nvidia trades at even 8 times sales at the end of fiscal 2028 and achieves $742 billion in revenue, its market cap could reach almost $6 trillion. That's 60% higher than its current market cap, suggesting that the stock could deliver respectable gains over the coming year.

So, buying this AI stock after its latest results could be a smart move, as 2027 could be a much better year for Nvidia.

#3082. With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

Higher borrowing costs aren't the whole story. Here's what to consider before putting your house hunt on hold.

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

While CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

To cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

But new data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

Pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

Whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.)

Think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

#3079. Is Tilray a Buy at Its Record Low, or Is It a Value Trap?

Tilray’s recent record revenue wasn’t as impressive as it seemed at first glance.

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:51PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Tilray Brands ›

The cannabis industry has been a massive disappointment in recent years, and even most industry leaders haven't escaped the bloodbath. Take, for instance, Tilray Brands (TLRY -8.70%), one of the largest players in the Canadian cannabis market. Tilray has significantly underperformed the broader market over the past half-decade, losing more than 90% of its value. The company is now near record lows. Is Tilray stock a buy at current levels, or would investors be catching a falling knife?

Tilray Brands faces a difficult regulatory landscape in the cannabis market. Recreational use of the substance remains illegal at the federal level in the U.S. It is legal in Canada, where the company is headquartered, but that market has its own challenges.

Obtaining the proper licenses in Canada is a complex and time-consuming process. The market north of the border is also characterized by stiff competition and persistent supply gluts. Although Tilray is an industry leader, these problems have harmed its financial results. The company has diversified its business in response.

It now operates four segments: cannabis, beverage, wellness (which offers a variety of products, including hemp-based foods), and distribution (which focuses on selling pharmaceutical products in certain international markets). But even a more diversified pool of operations has done little to improve Tilray's financial results.

In the first quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which ended on Aug. 31, Tilray's revenue increased by 23% year over year to a record $257 million. That looks impressive at first glance, but Tilray's top line did not grow that much organically. Earlier this year, it acquired certain assets associated with BrewDog, a craft brewery based in the United Kingdom.

This acquisition added $55.9 million in revenue to the company's total for the period. If we subtract that from Tilray's total revenue, its top line comes in at $201.2 million for the period, down about 4% year over year.

This includes cannabis revenue of $56.1 million, which dropped 13% year over year. Wellness revenue stayed roughly flat at $15.3 million, while distribution revenue was $84.3 million, 14% higher than the year-ago period. Beverage revenue minus the BrewDog acquisition declined 18% year over year to $45.6 million.

So of Tilray's four business segments, only one posted strong year-over-year organic sales growth. Meanwhile, the company's operating loss was $24.1 million, compared with $2.1 million in operating income in the year-ago period. It also turned in a net loss per share of $0.32, after breaking even in the comparable period of the previous fiscal year.

Tilray's poor financial results aren't the only problem. The company also faces a highly uncertain future, even given recent regulatory progress in the U.S. The federal government reclassified certain medical cannabis products and has discussed broader reclassification, which could encompass recreational cannabis.

But the substance remains illegal at the federal level. That means it still cannot be transported across state lines, among other restrictions. So, Tilray's opportunities in the U.S. remain severely limited. Will that change anytime soon? It's hard to say. Nobody knows if or when the U.S. will legalize recreational use of cannabis at the federal level.

Even if it does, Tilray might face problems similar to those it faced in Canada. What about other countries? Could Tilray bounce back by tapping into international markets? Unfortunately, that also seems unlikely. For instance, Germany legalized recreational cannabis in 2024, but this did very little to boost Tilray's results, despite the company's presence in the country.

Germany allowed people to grow cannabis at home (within certain limits) or join non-commercial cannabis clubs. The law left little room for commercial companies like Tilray. So, the pot grower faces a stringent regulatory environment practically wherever it goes, and that might not change anytime soon. Tilray is unlikely to bounce back.

Investing in the stock, even at its record low, isn't worth the trouble.

The recently renovated Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort offers great views, a well-equipped fitness center and delicious food.

Hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

For lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

#3077. Southside Bancshares: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Rising deposit costs will soon test whether the bank's yield gains can offset funding pressure in the quarters ahead.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:53PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Southside Bancshares ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 29, 2026, Southside Bancshares (SBSI -0.97%) announced net income of $28 million. Expanding lending yields and disciplined deposit pricing continue to cushion bank profitability across Texas metro growth markets.

Three key takeaways from management's comments stand out for long-term investors.

Commercial real estate payoffs offset new loan production during the third quarter. Management slowed its full-year loan growth outlook to low to mid single digits to account for ongoing property paydowns.

Net interest margin, the gap between interest earned on assets and interest paid on deposits, expanded as higher benchmark rates filtered into floating-rate debt. With over half the loan portfolio repricing every quarter, higher yields quickly boost interest earnings.

Certificates of deposit, which are fixed-rate time deposits, represent an upcoming funding cost pressure as fixed terms mature. Management plans to raise deposit rates selectively to retain customer balances while competition for liquidity intensifies.

Regional economic expansion across Texas markets provides a tailwind for commercial lending, and management isn't hiding its optimism about local credit conditions. Solid liquidity lines and low nonperforming assets support growth while management monitors deposit pricing discipline.

Expanding commercial relationships brings in low-cost operational deposits to reinforce long-term balance sheet stability.

#3075. Defense Stocks Fell After the Midterms. Here’s the 1 Defense Name I’d Buy Anyway -- and Why It Isn’t Lockheed Martin.

RTX is positioned to do well regardless of the political climate.

By James Halley – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:05PM EST

The midterm election results sent a shudder through the defense industry.

President Donald Trump is proposing a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027, but time is running out to pass the budget in a lame-duck Congress. Next year's Congress is likely to take a more critical look at defense spending.

RTX (RTX -1.32%) is one of only two major U.S.-based defense stocks whose shares have risen since the midterm elections. There are four reasons why RTX is the one defense stock I'd buy over Lockheed Martin (LMT -1.11%).

Unlike many of its peers, the company is positioned to continue doing well because its revenue streams also include sales of parts and equipment to commercial airlines, providing a cushion if next year's Congress slashes the defense budget.

RTX has three segments, but only one of them is a pure-play defense segment: Raytheon, which makes air and missile defense systems. The other two segments, Pratt & Whitney and Collins Aerospace, make defense and commercial airline products. Pratt & Whitney makes aircraft engines for civilian and military aircraft, while its Collins Aerospace segment makes aircraft systems, including avionics, navigation systems, and flight controls for commercial and defense aircraft.

Lockheed Martin's shares, on the other hand, are down more than 3% since the elections because it has little commercial sales, with more than 69% of its revenue coming from the U.S. government.

RTX reported double-digit revenue and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) growth in the third quarter. Revenue was reported as $25 billion, up 11% year over year, and adjusted EPS grew by 33% over the prior year to $2.26. The company also raised full-year guidance. It says it expects 2026 sales of $97 billion to $97.5 billion, up from earlier estimates of between $95 billion and $96 billion. It also raised adjusted EPS from $7.10 to $7.25, up to $7.65–$7.75.

Adjusted segment operating margins expanded by 310 basis points in the third quarter, and because aircraft engine maintenance and spare parts carry higher profit margins than initial equipment sales, RTX's installed base of commercial engines and avionics acts as a compounding cash-flow machine independent of Capitol Hill.

Pratt & Whitney's commercial aftermarket sales jumped 21% year over year, while Collins Aerospace's adjusted operating profit surged 50%.

Lockheed Martin also had a strong quarter, with revenue rising 11% year over year, to $20.7 billion and EPS of $7.97, up 14% from the same period last year. However, because so much of its revenue lately is tied to Iran war spending, that could slow at any time.

RTX reported a backlog of $340 billion in the third quarter, including $164 billion in defense sales and $176 billion in commercial sales. That provides a great deal of stability for investors looking at the company's long-term potential, as it represents three years' worth of revenue.

Just in the third quarter, Raytheon booked nearly $59 billion in defense awards, including production contracts for Tomahawk missiles and air-to-air missiles. Even with Democrats soon to control Congress, global demand for air defense and munitions makes these multiyear contracts highly resilient.

Lockheed Martin's backlog is smaller at $292 billion, and all of that is tied to defense contracts.

The company raised its quarterly dividend by 7.4% this year to $0.73 per share, the 32nd consecutive year it has increased its dividend. The dividend yield is an above-average 1.42%, and while that's lower than Lockheed Martin's 2.39% yield, RTX's streak of raising dividends is eight years longer.

In addition, over the past three years, RTX has increased its dividend by more than 23%, while Lockheed has raised its dividend by just over 9%.

RTX stands out as a stronger buy than Lockheed Martin right now largely because its balanced business model insulates it from post-midterm political turbulence on Capitol Hill.

RTX's greater commercial footprint not only provides a steady buffer against congressional scrutiny, but also fuels a high-margin aftermarket engine and spare-parts business that acts as a compounding cash-flow engine independent of Pentagon appropriations.

Atmos Rewards offers six communities, each with its own travel perks and opportunities to earn bonus points

Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

They’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

You can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

Joining a community is easy: Log in to your Atmos Rewards account and navigate to “Account overview.” Select “Join a Community,” browse the options and click the “Join” button under the one you choose.

Each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:

Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

New lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

Global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:

Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

If you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

This community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:

This community would be an excellent choice if your upcoming travels include several of these airports, even if dining isn't the main reason for your trips. If dining out is one of your favorite activities, check out the best credit cards for restaurants.

Active Escapes focuses on airports in outdoor-oriented destinations that are all in the U.S., save one. Benefits here are:

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:

While these airports are gateways to national parks and other natural attractions, you don’t have to be an outdoor enthusiast to benefit. Like before, don’t let the heading sway you. Rather, consider the destinations before you decide.

Families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:

Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, these destinations qualify for bonus points and status points:

This community may be especially valuable if you regularly book award flights for children 12 and under. Even if you don't travel with kids, it could be worth considering if its qualifying airports align better with your travel plans than those of other communities.

Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:

Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

Two Travel Now discounts per year for 30% off one-way refundable Y-class fares on Alaska Airlines, booked within four days of departure for travel to, from or within Alaska.

Ship cargo within Alaska for $49 plus tax (weight, size and content limits apply).

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Baggage benefits don’t combine with other free checked bag allowances, such as those that come with some Alaska credit cards. However, they apply to everyone traveling on the same reservation.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus offers:

While this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel plans — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

Hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:

Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

Earn 50% more points and status points on flights between Hawaiian islands beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

The 10 destinations eligible for bonus points through Dec. 31, 2027 are:

Seven destinations are in Hawaii, with one on the mainland and two international cities. If you live in Hawaii and like to hop between islands, this community is a strong choice.

Don’t be persuaded by the names of the communities. Look a little deeper, because there’s a lot of overlap between destination lists. Compare the options against your upcoming travel plans.

You can change communities once per calendar year, so you aren’t locked in to your initial choice indefinitely. However, switching communities resets your destination-challenge progress, but you’ll retain any points you’ve already earned.

If your home airport (or one you visit frequently) is already on a community’s list, you may have an easier time earning points. Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

Finally, pay attention to airport codes. For example, Tokyo’s Narita (NRT) and Haneda (HND) appear on different community lists. New York’s qualifying airport is JFK, while it is DCA in Washington, D.C. If you have a choice between airports, check which one qualifies for your community’s challenge.
